description: HIERARCHICAL NAVIGATION CONFIG — Static room topology and door information for Dijkstra-based path planning
comment: Fully-known environment with actual room centers, entry points (doors) from Webots world, and hallway costs. This file defines the graph structure used by the 3-layer hierarchical planner.
================== WHAT THIS FILE DOES =: This JSON file contains the complete house topology used for hierarchical path planning. Instead of using A* grid search over thousands of cells, the hierarchical system plans at the room level using Dijkstra's algorithm on a small graph of ~5 rooms, then generates waypoints for each room transition.

================== STRUCTURE OVERVIEW ==.rooms: Dictionary of all rooms in the house. Each room has: center (room's central point), entry_points (list of doors where robot can enter/exit), bounds (axis-aligned box around room), type (hallway/room), size (dimensions)
================== STRUCTURE OVERVIEW ==.hallways: List of [room_A, room_B, cost] connections. Cost represents traversal difficulty (higher = prefer alternative routes). All hallways currently cost 1.5 (uniform - could be optimized for obstacles/furniture)

LOADED_BY: nav_agent_v2.py: __init__() loads this file at startup from: controllers/nao_assist_controller/house/hierarchical_config.json
hierarchical_planner.py: HierarchicalPlanner.load_house_config() parses the rooms and hallways into graph structures
PLANNING_FLOW: 3. Planner Layer 1: TopologicalGraph.dijkstra() finds room-level path using hallway costs
4. Planner Layer 2: RoomPathPlanner.plan_room_sequence() generates waypoints by connecting entry points
5. WaypointController.execute() moves robot along waypoints with sonar avoidance

CALL_CHAIN_DETAILED.Which_Uses: entry_points to generate waypoints between rooms

ROOMS.center: [x, y] — Central point of room used as waypoint in hierarchical planning. Example: corridor center is [-0.36, -0.32]
ROOMS.entry_points: [[x1, y1], [x2, y2], ...] — Doors where robot transitions between this room and adjacent rooms. Multiple entry_points allow flexible entrance/exit angles. Example: kitchen has 2 entry points on its shared wall with corridor: [[1.84, 1.40], [1.84, 0.40]]
ROOMS.bounds: [x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max] — Axis-aligned bounding box of room. Used for line-of-sight checks and boundary validation when generating waypoints
ROOMS.type: hallway | room — Type descriptor (currently informational, not used by planner)
ROOMS.door_frame: ID reference to door frame in Webots world (used by doorway_detector.py for alignment)

================== HALLWAYS ARRAY REFERE.COST_MEANING: Dijkstra distance metric for traversing this hallway. Currently all costs are 1.5 (uniform). Could be optimized: increase cost for narrow/cluttered paths, decrease for open paths
================== HALLWAYS ARRAY REFERE.EXAMPLE: ['corridor', 'kitchen', 1.5] means: corridor ↔ kitchen hallway costs 1.5 units to traverse
================== HALLWAYS ARRAY REFERE.ALL_HALLWAYS_CONNECT_TO_CORRIDOR: In this house, all rooms connect to the central corridor. Hallway costs determine which path Dijkstra prefers if multiple routes exist

================== ENTRY_POINTS EXPLAINE.PURPOSE: Entry points are coordinates where the robot physically transitions between rooms. They represent doorways/passages.
================== ENTRY_POINTS EXPLAINE.WHY_MULTIPLE: A room may have multiple doors on the same wall. Entry points allow flexible entry angles. Example: kitchen has 2 entry points vertically spaced (y=1.40 and y=0.40), allowing robot to enter from different positions
HOW_THEY_RE_USED: 1. RoomPathPlanner finds nearest entry point to robot's current position
2. Generates waypoint at entry point to transition between rooms
3. WaypointController moves robot toward these waypoint entry points
4. NavAgent._PlannerAdapter maps world coordinates to nearest room by checking which entry point is closest
================== ENTRY_POINTS EXPLAINE.GEOMETRY: Entry points should align with actual door/passage locations in Webots world (extracted from world geometry when file was created)

================== ROOM_TARGETS SECTION.PURPOSE: Maps room IDs to human-readable labels and room properties
================== ROOM_TARGETS SECTION.LABEL: Human name displayed in logs and speech (e.g., 'Kitchen' in voice commands)
================== ROOM_TARGETS SECTION.FURNITURE: List of furniture items in room (informational, used by ObjectClassifier for semantic planning)
================== ROOM_TARGETS SECTION.DOORS: List of door IDs that provide access to this room (used for routing/blocking analysis)

================== DATA FLOW DIAGRAM ===: Layer 2 Waypoints: Extract entry_points, center coords
ROBOT MOVES along waypoints, avoiding obstacles with sonar

================== IMPORTANT NOTES =====.ENTRY_POINTS_ARE_CRITICAL: Planner cannot generate valid paths without entry_points. If entry_points are wrong, robot will aim for incorrect waypoints and may hit walls
================== IMPORTANT NOTES =====.ALL_HALLWAY_COSTS_UNIFORM: Current design has all hallway costs = 1.5. This means Dijkstra treats all room-to-room transitions equally. Could optimize by: increasing cost for narrow hallways, decreasing for wide open areas
================== IMPORTANT NOTES =====.ROOM_CENTERS_SHOULD_BE_OPEN: Room centers should be inside the room, not near walls. Used as intermediate waypoint.
================== IMPORTANT NOTES =====.BOUNDS_USED_FOR_LOS_CHECKS: RoomPathPlanner may use bounds for line-of-sight validation (though currently just uses straight-line waypoints)
================== IMPORTANT NOTES =====.NO_DYNAMIC_UPDATES: This config is static (loaded once at startup). Dynamic obstacles are handled by WaypointController's reactive avoidance, not by replanning with new config
================== IMPORTANT NOTES =====.EXTRACTED_FROM_WEBOTS: These values were extracted from worlds/My project.wbt. If world geometry changes, this file should be regenerated
